prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1400; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant after a rear-end collision at a traffic light. Claimant states they were stopped when their vehicle was struck from behind and reports shoulder pain since the impact. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been asked to keep receipts for all treatment.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record. The driver involved is named on the policy and coverage was in force on the date of loss. No issues with the policy identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Their account of the collision matches what they described when the claim was first reported. They gave the same sequence of events and were clear about where each vehicle ended up.

Entry 4: Obtained the police report. It confirms the collision occurred as described and records the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene. The responding officer noted no conflicting statements.

Entry 5: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the rear impact and the stopped position of the claimant's vehicle. Their account is consistent with the claimant's.

Entry 6: Received scene photos and two witness statements. Both witnesses describe the same sequence and the photos show the damage pattern expected from a rear impact.

Entry 7: Inspected the vehicle. The damage is located where the described impact would be expected and its severity fits the reported collision. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 8: Checked prior claim history for the claimant. No earlier injury to the shoulder or neck area appears in the records available to us.

Entry 9: Claimant has provided medical records showing a shoulder injury consistent with the force of a collision of this type. The injury type is a common result of this kind of impact.

Entry 10: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested updated treatment notes from the treating provider to review the reasons for the extended course of care.

Entry 11: Claim remains open pending receipt of the updated treatment notes. Nothing reviewed so far suggests the damage or injury predates the start of coverage. Next review scheduled once the notes arrive.
